reconcile.note: Gill, following Godwin and Hammond, argues that ancient hour-names spanned three-hour blocks, so Mark's third hour and John's sixth hour could describe the same crucifixion window.

discrepancy.note: Strauss treats the third-hour and sixth-hour timings as a genuine contradiction that no reading of the hour-reckoning removes.

quotes.text: according to Mark it was the third hour ὥρα τρίτη (nine in the morning) when Jesus was crucified ( v. 25 ). On the other hand, John says ( xix. 14 ) that it was about the sixth hour (when according to Mark Jesus had already hung three hours on the cross) that Pilate first sat in judgment over him.
quotes.attr: David Friedrich Strauss (d. 1874), The Life of Jesus Critically Examined, trans. George Eliot (1846), ch. on the crucifixion, on Mark 15:25 and John 19:14.

sides.snippet: It was the third hour, and they crucified him.
sides.verseText: It was the third hour, and they crucified him.

sides.snippet: Now it was the Preparation Day of the Passover, at about the sixth hour.
sides.verseText: Now it was the Preparation Day of the Passover, at about the sixth hour. He said to the Jews, \"Behold, your King!\"
